maya: quick recap from the continuous-batching sweep I ran this morning across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. wanted to capture the kernel-selection + kv-cache observations and propose conservative per-GPU targets for max_batch_size and max_tokens_per_batch. TL;DR: set per-card max_tokens targets (not just max_batch_size) — kernel fit + kv fragmentation drive worst-case latency more than raw batch count.

maya: key datapoints:
- workload: mix of chat+streaming gen, seq_len distribution median=64, p95=512.
- profiler: CPU->GPU queueing spikes co-occur with large KV-frag on H100 when aggregated tokens > ~180k per device.
- kernels: H100 picks v2 attention kernel at certain seq_len shapes; if batch tokens cross a boundary, it falls back to slower kernel, latency jumps ~18-25%.
- A100 shows more graceful degradation but KV cache fragmentation still causes 6-8% extra time at p95 when max_tokens_per_batch too high.

maya: my conservative recommendations (start canary, 24h):
- A10: max_batch_size=48, max_tokens_per_batch=120k
- T4: max_batch_size=32, max_tokens_per_batch=90k
- L4: max_batch_size=40, max_tokens_per_batch=100k
- A100: max_batch_size=64, max_tokens_per_batch=160k (keep slower kernel boundary in mind)
- H100: max_batch_size=80, max_tokens_per_batch=140k (lower than A100 due to KV-frag + kernel swings)

maya: experiment notes (commands used):
```bash
./run_bench --model gpt-large --seq-dist "med:64,p95:512" --profile --device A100 --max-tokens 200000
```
and the profiler marker I used: `RT:batch_form:tokens` which shows token aggregation per GPU per 1s window.

sam: nice writeup. question: how did you measure the kernel switch boundary? is it reproducible with fixed shapes?

maya: yes — I forced constant shape runs (pad to 256 / 512) and checked the kernel selection trace. extracted from logs: `kernel_select: attention_v2 (fast)` vs `attention_fallback` with timestamps. reproducible when aggregated tokens per call exceed ~X shape threshold which matches the fallback.

perf-bot: perf job 2026-03-01-0923 completed. A100 throughput baseline regression +2.3% p95 compared to yesterday's commit. Job id: perf-20260301-0923.

alex: +1 on conservative H100 cap. we should also add a temporary kernel selection guard in the runtime: if predicted aggregate tokens near fallback boundary, prefer smaller batches (or split) to avoid fallback.

jordan: question on operational impact: lowering max_tokens on H100 from 180k->140k will increase request dispatches. what's the expected NA cost delta?

maya: rough calc: for our median mix, it increases GPU call count ~6-9% but reduces p95 tail failures and avoids expensive fallback. net cost delta estimated ~+1.8% but p95 latency drops ~12% and SLO breach probability down a lot. tradeoff seems worth it for customer-facing routes.

sam: can we make the per-route policy opt-in initially? e.g., high-ttl customer traffic keep looser caps?

maya: yes — rollout plan: patch configs in infra-config repo with per-cardset defaults and route-level overrides. default conservative set goes to all envs; add `max_tokens_override` for routes. patch diff looks like:
```yaml
cardset_defaults:
  H100:
    max_batch_size: 80
    max_tokens_per_batch: 140000
route_overrides:
  /chat/streaming/*:
    max_tokens_per_batch: 180000 # opt-in until canary proves safe
```

alex: love the route override. also suggest adding a runtime log line when a request is split due to kernel-boundary avoidance (helps debug customer tickets).

jordan: +1. also can we add a quick perf test matrix to the canary job so it asserts no >5% regression in p95 for any card?

maya: yep, will update the canary job. plan:
- push config PR by EOD
- run 24h canary on a subset (us-west H100/A100 + eu-west L4)
- perf-bot will run matrix and post results.

sam: thanks — will run the kernel-selector probe on staging later today and post results here. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all. ping me if you want raw traces, I uploaded them to s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1755559876/ (contains flamegraphs + kernel_select logs).

maya: followups: add a short TODO to fix KV fragmentation via more aggressive compaction in runtime (tracked separately).
